items.title: Irreducible (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An element of a ring is called irreducible if it cannot be written as a product of two non-units.

items.title: Invertible (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An invertible fractional ideal is a fractional ideal that has an inverse in the monoid of fractional ideals under multiplication.

items.title: Injective module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An injective module is one with the property that maps from submodules to it can be extended to larger modules.

items.title: Initial ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. In a graded ring, the initial ideal of an ideal I is the set of all homogeneous components of minimal degree of the elements in I (this is an ideal of the multiplicative monoid…

items.title: Inertia group (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An inertia group is a group of automorphisms of a ring whose elements fix a given prime ideal and act trivially on the corresponding residue class ring.

items.title: Indecomposable (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A module is called indecomposable if it is not the direct sum of two proper submodules.

items.title: Incomparability property (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The extension A⊆B is said to satisfy the incomparability property if whenever Q and Q' are distinct primes of B lying over prime P in A, then Q⊈Q' and Q'⊈Q.

items.title: Idealwise separated (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A module $M$ is idealwise separated for an ideal I if for every ideal, ${\mathfrak {a}}$, $\bigcap _{n\geq 1}I^{n}({\mathfrak {a}}\otimes M)=0$ (for example, this is the case when…

items.title: Hull (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An injective hull (or envelope) of a module is a minimal injective module containing it.

items.title: Height (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. The height of a prime ideal, also called its codimension or rank or altitude, is the supremum of the lengths of chains of prime ideals descending from it.

items.title: Gröbner basis (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Gröbner basis is a set of generators for an ideal of a polynomial ring satisfying certain conditions.

items.title: Graded algebra (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A graded algebra or module is one that is a direct sum of pieces indexed by an abelian group, often the group of integers.

items.title: Going up property (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An extension R⊆S of commutative rings is said to have the going up property if whenever p1⊆p2 is a chain of prime ideals in R and q1 is a prime ideal of S with q1∩R=p1, there is…

items.title: Going down property (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An extension R⊆S of commutative rings is said to have the going down property if whenever p1⊆p2 is a chain of prime ideals in R and q2 is a prime ideal of S with q2∩R=p2, there…

items.title: Geometrically regular (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The word "geometrically" usually refers to properties that continue to hold after taking finite field extensions. For example, a ring R over a field k is called geometrically norma…

items.title: GCD (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. Abbreviation for greatest common divisor

items.title: Gaussian ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Gaussian ring is the ring of Gaussian integers m+ni.

items.title: G-ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An alternative name for a Grothendieck ring.

items.title: Fractionary ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An alternative name for fractional ideals

items.title: Fractional ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: If K is the ring of fractions of an integral domain R, then a fractional ideal of R is a submodule of the R-module K contained in kR for some k in K.

items.title: Formally smooth (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A homomorphism f:A→B of rings is called formally smooth, formally unramified, or formally etale if for every A-algebra R with a nilpotent ideal I, the natural map from HomA(R/I,…

items.title: Flat module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A flat module is a module such that tensoring with it preserves exactness.

items.title: Fitting ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Fitting ideal In(M) of a module M generated by g elements is the ideal generated by the determinants of the minors of size g–n of the matrix of relations defining the module.

items.title: Finitely generated (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A module over a ring is called finitely generated if every element is a linear combination of a fixed finite number of elements. If the module happens to be an algebra this is m…

items.title: Finite type (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An algebra over a ring is said to be of finite type if it is finitely generated as an algebra.

items.title: Finite field (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A finite module (or algebra) over a ring usually means one that is finitely generated as a module. It may also mean one with a finite number of elements, especially in the term fin…

items.title: Faithfully flat module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A faithfully flat module over a ring R is a flat module whose tensor product with any non-zero module is non-zero.

items.title: Faithful module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A faithful module is a module whose annihilator is 0.

items.title: Factorial ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Factorial ring is an alternative name for a unique factorization domain.

items.title: Face ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An alternative name for a Stanley–Reisner ring.

items.title: Extension of an ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An extension of an ideal is the ideal generated by the image under a homomorphism of rings.

items.title: Ext functors (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Ext functors, the derived functors of the Hom functor.

items.title: Excellent ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An excellent ring is a universally catenary Grothendieck ring such that for every finitely generated algebra the singular points of the spectrum form a closed subset.

items.title: Exact zero divisor (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A zero divisor $x$ is said to be an exact zero divisor if its annihilator, $\operatorname {Ann} _{R}(x)=\{r\in R\mid rx=0\}$, is a principal ideal $yR$ whose annihilator is $xR$:…

items.title: Euclidean domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Euclidean domain is an integral domain with a form of Euclid's algorithm.

items.title: étale (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A morphism of rings is called étale if it is formally etale and locally finitely presented.

items.title: Essentially of finite type (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An algebra is said to be essentially of finite type over another algebra if it is a localization of a finitely generated algebra.

items.title: Essential submodule (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A submodule M of N is called an essential submodule if it intersects every nonzero submodule of N.

items.title: Equicharacteristic (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A local ring is called equicharacteristic if it has the same characteristic as its residue field.

items.title: Embedded (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An embedded prime of a module is a non-minimal associated prime.

items.title: Dualizing (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. Grothendieck local duality is a duality for cohomology of modules over a local ring.

items.title: Dominate (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A local ring B is said to dominate a local ring A if it contains A and the maximal ideal of B contains the maximal ideal of A.

items.title: Divisorial ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A divisorial ideal of an integral domain is a non-zero fractional ideal that is an intersection of principal fractional ideals.

items.title: Divisor (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A divisor of an integral domain is an equivalence class of non-zero fractional ideals, where two such ideals are called equivalent if they are contained in the same principal fr…

items.title: Divisible module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A divisible module is a module such that multiplication by any regular element of the ring is surjective.

items.title: Discrete valuation ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A discrete valuation ring is an integrally closed Noetherian local ring of dimension 1.

items.title: Deviation of a local ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A deviation of a local ring is an invariant that measures how far the ring is from being regular.

items.title: Determinantal ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: This often refers to properties of an ideal generated by determinants of minors of a matrix. For example, a determinantal ring is generated by the entries of a matrix, with relatio…

items.title: Determinant module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The determinant module of a module is the top exterior power of the module.

items.title: Derived normal ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The derived normal ring of an integral domain is its integral closure in its quotient field.

items.title: Derivation (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An additive homomorphism d from a ring to a module that satisfies Leibniz's rule d(ab)=ad(b)+bd(a).

items.title: Depth (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The I-depth (also called grade) of a module M over a ring R, where I is an ideal, is the smallest integer n such that Extn R(R/I,M) is nonzero. When I is the maximal ideal of a loc…

items.title: Dedekind domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Dedekind domain is a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension at most 1.

items.title: Decomposition group (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A decomposition group is a group of automorphisms of a ring whose elements fix a given prime ideal.

items.title: Decomposable (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A module is called decomposable if it can be written as a direct sum of two non-zero submodules.

items.title: Cox ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Cox ring is a sort of universal homogeneous coordinate ring for a projective variety.

items.title: Cotangent space (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The cotangent space of a local ring with maximal ideal m is the vector space m/m2 over the residue field.

items.title: Coprime (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. Two ideals are called coprime if their sum is the whole ring.

items.title: Coprimary module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A coprimary module is a module with exactly one associated prime.

items.title: Contraction of an ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The contraction of an ideal is the ideal given by the inverse image of some ideal under a homomorphism of rings.

items.title: Constructible subset (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: For a Noetherian ring, a constructible subset of the spectrum is one that is a finite union of locally closed sets. For rings that are not Noetherian the definition of a constructi…

items.title: Conormal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The conormal module of a quotient of a ring by an ideal I is the module I/I2.

items.title: Connected (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A graded algebra over a field k is connected if its 0th degree component is k.

items.title: Congruence ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A congruence ideal of a surjective homomorphism f: B→C of commutative rings is the image under f of the annihilator of the kernel of f.

items.title: Conductor (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The conductor of an integral domain R is the annihilator of the R-module T/R, where T is the integral closure of R in its quotient field.

items.title: Composite (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A composite number is a positive integer that is neither prime nor 1.

items.title: Completion of a module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The completion of a module or ring M at an ideal I is the inverse limit of the modules M/InM.

items.title: Completely integrally closed (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A domain R is called completely integrally closed if, whenever all positive powers of some element x of the quotient field are contained in a finitely generated R-module, x is in R…

items.title: Complete (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A local complete intersection ring is a Noetherian local ring whose completion is the quotient of a regular local ring by an ideal generated by a regular sequence.

items.title: Coherent (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A module is called coherent if it is finitely generated and every homomorphism to it from a finitely generated module has a finitely generated kernel.

items.title: Cohen–Macaulay (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A local ring is called Cohen–Macaulay if it is Noetherian and the Krull dimension is equal to the depth. A ring is called Cohen–Macaulay if it is Noetherian and all localization…

items.title: Codimension (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The codimension of a prime ideal is another name for its height.

items.title: Codepth (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The codepth of a finitely generated module over a Noetherian local ring is its dimension minus its depth.

items.title: CoCoA (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The CoCoA computer algebra system for computations in commutative algebra

items.title: Clean (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring R is called clean if it has a finite filtration all of whose quotients are of the form R/p for p an associated prime of M. A…

items.title: Characteristic of a ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The characteristic of a ring is a non-negative integer generating the Z-ideal of multiples of 1 that are zero.

items.title: Chain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A strictly increasing or decreasing sequence of prime ideals.

items.title: Catenary (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A ring is called catenary if for every two prime ideals, one contained in the other, all maximal chains between them have the same length.

items.title: Canonical (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: "Canonical module" is an alternative term for a dualizing module.

items.title: Buchsbaum ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Buchsbaum ring is a Noetherian local ring such that every system of parameters is a weak sequence.

items.title: Bourbaki ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Bourbaki ideal of a torsion-free module M is an ideal isomorphic (as a module) to a torsion-free quotient of M by a free submodule.

items.title: Boolean ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Boolean ring is a ring such that x2=x for all x.

items.title: Big (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The word "big" when applied to a module emphasizes that the module is not necessarily finitely generated. In particular a big Cohen–Macaulay module is a module that has a system of…

items.title: Bézout domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Bézout domain is an integral domain in which the sum of two principal ideals is a principal ideal.

items.title: Bass number (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: If M is a module over a local ring R with residue field k, then the ith Bass number of M is the k-dimension of Exti R(k,M).

items.title: Associated prime (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An associated prime of a module M over a ring R is a prime ideal p such that M has a submodule isomorphic to R/p.

items.title: ASL (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Acronym for algebra with straightening law.

items.title: Annihilator (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The annihilator of a subset of a module is the ideal of elements whose product with any element of the subset is 0.

items.title: Analytically (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: This often refers to properties of the completion of a local ring; cf. formally

items.title: Analytic (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. The analytic spread of an ideal of a local ring is the Krull dimension of the fiber at the special point of the local ring of the Rees algebra of the ideal.

items.title: Almost (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An element x of a ring is called almost integral over a subring if there is a regular element a of the subring so that axn is in the subring for all positive integers n.

items.title: Algebraic-geometrical local ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A local ring that is a localization of a finitely-generated domain over a field.

items.title: Affine ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An affine ring R over another ring S (often a field) is a ring (or sometimes an integral domain) that is finitely generated over S.

items.title: Adic (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The I-adic topology on a ring has a base of neighborhoods of 0 given by powers of the ideal I.

items.title: Acceptable ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Acceptable rings are generalizations of excellent rings, with the conditions about regular rings in the definition replaced by conditions about Gorenstein rings.

items.title: Absolutely (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The word "absolutely" usually means "not relatively"; i.e., independent of the base field in some sense. It is often synonymous with "geometrically".

items.title: Absolute integral closure (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The absolute integral closure is the integral closure of an integral domain in an algebraic closure of the field of fractions of the domain.

items.title: Zero vector (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: The additive identity in a vector space. In a normed vector space, it is the unique vector of norm zero. In a Euclidean vector space, it is the unique vector of length zero.[18]

items.title: Vector (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction.

items.title: Unit vector (linear algebra)
items.excerpt: a vector in a normed vector space whose norm is 1, or a Euclidean vector of length one.[15]
